title: Finite Tor amplitude of locally constant perfect duals
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p
e\ell$, and let $S$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $\Lambda$ be one of the admissible condensed coefficient rings $A,\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathcal O_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, where $A$ is finite commutative and killed by a power of $\ell$ and $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ is finite [sk-def-localizing-closure]. Put $R=\Lambda(*)$ and $B=\Lambda_S$. Suppose $P\in D(S_{\mathrm{proét}},B)$ has a pro-étale cover $\{U_i	o S\}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] on which it is the termwise scalar extension $B|_{U_i}\otimes_{\underline R}\underline{F_i^ ullet}$ of a bounded complex of finite projective $R$-modules [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex, def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package], where underlines denote constant sheaves. Form $P^\vee=R\mathcal Hom_B(P,B)$ using relative derived internal Hom [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]. There exist integers $a\le b$ such that, for every sheaf $N$ of $B$-modules in degree zero,
$$H^q(P\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}N)=0\quad(q
otin[a,b]),\qquad H^q(P^\vee\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}N)=0\quad(q
otin[-b,-a]).$$
In particular both objects have finite Tor amplitude [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. For $S=\varnothing$ one can take $a=b=0$.

proof.text: Apply the module-object/ringed-site derived comparison to $B=\Lambda_S$. It preserves the underlying abelian sheaves, relative derived tensor, internal Hom and slice restrictions. Work with its section-ring sheaf, still denoted $B$; this does not identify $B$ with the discrete constant sheaf $\underline R$.

source.place: Paragraph 2, final sentence (locally constant perfect coefficient dual); paragraph 3, parenthetical assertion that the perfect factors lie in Dctf: extracted uniform-Tor-bound part.

proof.text: If $S=\varnothing$, the empty covering forces every module sheaf to be zero, so take $a=b=0$. Otherwise finite type over $\operatorname{Spec}k$ gives quasi-compactness. Apply the finite scalar-perfect refinement lemma to the cover and models in the hypothesis. It supplies a finite nonempty cover $\{V_j\}$, scalar-extended complexes $E_j^\bullet\simeq P|_{V_j}$, their degreewise finite-free splittings and intervals $[a_j,b_j]\subseteq[a,b]$, where $a=\min a_j$, $b=\max b_j$. These choices precede every test sheaf.

source.place: Paragraph 2, final sentence (locally constant perfect coefficient dual); paragraph 3, parenthetical assertion that the perfect factors lie in Dctf: extracted uniform-Tor-bound part.

proof.text: On each slice put $B_j=B|_{V_j}$. Internal Hom restriction identifies $P^\vee|_{V_j}$ with $R\mathcal Hom_{B_j}(E_j^\bullet,B_j[0])$. Apply the split-perfect dual Tor-window lemma with $a_j,b_j$: it supplies the signed dual $D_j^n=\mathcal Hom_{B_j}(E_j^{-n},B_j)$, $d^n(\phi)=(-1)^{n+1}\phi d_{E_j}^{-n-1}$, its dualized finite-free splittings, the K-injective comparison, flatness of both complexes, and the two Tor bounds for every $B_j$-module sheaf. Thus $P|_{V_j}$ has Tor amplitude in $[a_j,b_j]\subseteq[a,b]$ and $P^\vee|_{V_j}$ in $[-b_j,-a_j]\subseteq[-b,-a]$.

source.place: Paragraph 2, final sentence (locally constant perfect coefficient dual); paragraph 3, parenthetical assertion that the perfect factors lie in Dctf: extracted uniform-Tor-bound part.

proof.text: Apply clause (i) of cover-local Tor detection to $P$ with $[a,b]$ and to $P^\vee$ with $[-b,-a]$. It gives the required global vanishings for every degree-zero sheaf $N$: exact slice restriction commutes with cohomology and derived tensor, and the covering detects vanishing of those cohomology sheaves. The comparison of step 1 preserves these sheaves, so the same bounds hold for the original module objects. By the definition of Tor amplitude both objects have finite Tor amplitude.
